items.followUp: State two functions of stems in plants.

rubric.why: Roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.

rubric.why: Roots hold the plant firmly in the soil.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that roots anchor or hold the plant in the soil.

modelAnswer: Roots absorb water and mineral salts from the soil.
Roots anchor the plant firmly in the soil.

items.followUp: Name the three types of plastids and state one function of each.

rubric.why: Plastids are double-membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for defining plastids as membrane-bound organelles found in plant cells.

rubric.why: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chloroplasts and stating their chlorophyll or photosynthesis association.

rubric.why: Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming chromoplasts and stating that they contain pigments or give colour.

rubric.why: Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming leucoplasts and stating that they are colourless or store food.

modelAnswer: Plastids are double-membrane-bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of plant cells.
Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carry out photosynthesis.
Chromoplasts contain pigments that give colour to plant parts.
Leucoplasts are colourless plastids that store food.
The three types of plastids are chloroplasts, chromoplasts and leucoplasts.

items.followUp: Give two characteristics of kingdom Monera and two of kingdom Protista.

rubric.why: Organisms in kingdom Monera are unicellular.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Monerans are unicellular.

rubric.why: Monerans are prokaryotic and lack a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Monerans are prokaryotic or lack a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Protists are eukaryotic and have a true nucleus.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that protists are eukaryotic or have a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Protists are mostly unicellular; many are aquatic, and examples include algae and protozoa.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that protists are mostly unicellular, are aquatic, or include algae and protozoa.

modelAnswer: Kingdom Monera consists of unicellular prokaryotes that lack a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.
Bacteria, including cyanobacteria, belong to Monera.
Kingdom Protista consists mainly of unicellular eukaryotes with a true nucleus.
Many protists are aquatic; examples include algae and protozoa, and some move by cilia, flagella or pseudopodia.

items.followUp: Compare arteries and veins in terms of direction of blood flow, wall thickness, lumen and valves.

rubric.why: Veins carry blood towards the heart; capillaries connect arterioles to venules.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that veins carry blood towards the heart or that capillaries connect arterioles and venules.

rubric.why: Veins have relatively thin walls, while capillary walls are only one cell thick.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for comparing the walls of veins and capillaries, including the one-cell-thick capillary wall.

rubric.why: Veins have a wider lumen than capillaries, which have a very narrow lumen.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for comparing the wider vein lumen with the narrow capillary lumen.

rubric.why: Capillaries allow exchange of materials between blood and body tissues.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that capillaries enable exchange between blood and tissues.

rubric.why: Veins have valves to prevent backflow; capillaries do not have valves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly comparing valves in veins and capillaries.

modelAnswer: Veins carry blood towards the heart; capillaries connect arterioles to venules.
Veins have relatively thin walls, while capillary walls are only one cell thick.
Veins have a wider lumen; capillaries have a very narrow lumen.
Capillaries allow exchange of materials between the blood and body tissues.
Veins have valves to prevent backflow; capillaries do not have valves.
